title: Rabbit Lands HUD modernization explorations
intended_camera: existing elevated third-person gameplay camera, landscape 16:10

references.role: authoritative current gameplay composition and HUD
supporting original UI materials, icons, party and chat

variants.name: Heritage Polish
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a single full-screen high fidelity desktop MMORPG HUD design concept for Rabbit Lands.
Input images: Image 1 is the authoritative current IN-GAME SCENE and HUD reference. Image 2 is a supporting UI reference only for the game's current dark brown, warm brass, cream text, icon language and party/chat treatments; do not use its flat green background.
Primary request: modernize the HUD of Rabbit Lands, a stylized fantasy MMORPG, while keeping the game itself recognizable.
Scene/backdrop INVARIANTS: use precisely the elevated third-person/isometric gameplay framing in Image 1: small blue-clad player Kellan near the middle on gray cobblestone courtyard paving, a round gray stone tower at upper middle-left, dark foliage at upper left, and a dark roof entering foreground bottom middle. Preserve camera angle, courtyard geometry, scale of player, lighting and muted stylized game graphics. Do not replace the world with a scenic landscape, other game, close camera, photorealistic environment, or a bunny protagonist. The world should occupy most of the image, with HUD crisply overlaid.
Presentation: one polished finished playable gameplay-screen mockup, landscape aspect close to 16:10, high resolution, sharp readable interface typography, disciplined alignment, intentional iconography and spacing. Treat this as an interaction designer's plausible proposal, not marketing art. Components look usable at actual screen scale. Icons are fantasy game actions and objects. All panels and text inside safe edges. No monitor/device frame, no browser chrome, no multi-panel collage, no annotations, no captions or large concept title in image. Rabbit Lands identity; a small RL monogram is allowed, no other game logos.
Maintain the existing Rabbit Lands systems rather than inventing a new combat model: Health, Ether, Food, Load, Action points, Experience; quick items, spells, inventory, character, skills, crafting, journal, map, settings, chat, party and system messages. No invented required class, level 60, premium currency, battle pass or store advertisement. Example consistent values: Health 120/150, Ether 45/60, Food 42/45, Action 28/30, Load 115/320. Party names Kellan, Mira, Rowan. Chat short messages: "Tavi: Meet at the bridge.", "Rowan: Ready when you are.", "Ari: Buying Sunleaf." System message "Entered Four Gates." Area name "Four Gates". Any optional objective is a hypothetical UI example, "Meet at the bridge" with "Four Gates". Clear cream/white readable text, never tiny illegible decorative gibberish.

DESIGN 01, HERITAGE POLISH, only 15 percent change from current. This must visibly retain the original distinctive structure in reference 1: the full-width thin bottom strip containing all six horizontal colored meters ABOVE the long row of roughly 22 square fantasy utility/action buttons; the narrow full-height dark brown right-side rail with RL at top, 6 stacked item slots and abbreviated skill list in the middle, then the two circular blue time/compass instruments at bottom. Keep clear chat in the upper left and a separate small system log in lower left. Preserve current icon silhouettes and order as closely as possible. Keep tiny player name and four compact overhead bars above the player, but neaten them. Do NOT move everything to the center or transform it into a generic MMO.
Modernize execution: consistent thin brass strokes, simpler matte dark brown surfaces, crisper re-painted icons, unified subtle 4px corners, increased contrast and text baseline alignment, slightly reduced framing weight, restrained readable hover accent on one utility button. Right rail remains recognizable but cleanly spaced. Chat is transparent with a very subtle local fade behind readable cream text, channel colors restrained, one compact tab row and unobtrusive input underline. Visually near the current HUD, just much better finished and cleaner. No new minimap or objectives in this conservative option.
variants.review: Pass as a conservative visual exploration. Keeps original bottom strip, right rail, separate chat/system areas, and scene. Some generated numeric labels are illustrative; exact meter ordering and values require specification before implementation.

DESIGN 02, REFINED CLASSIC, 35 percent redesign. Keep the recognizable warm dark brown and antique brass fantasy aesthetic and familiar square painted icons, but release the full-height right rail and full-width bottom slab. Use classic PC MMO corners, not a center combat bar. Upper left: small horizontal player identity card "Kellan" with compact Health and Ether, three tiny secondary meters underneath; immediately below, three compact party rows. Lower left: tidy tabbed social chat on a low opacity warm gradient, a small separate System line above, no huge opaque box. Across BOTTOM LEFT TO MIDDLE: retain a long row of smaller familiar utility icons in logical groups, with six readable thin meters just above, but let it float with transparent gaps rather than fill the entire width. Lower RIGHT: a short 2 by 3 quick-item tray, a refined version of the original round compass/time instrument, and a very compact skills summary accessible behind a "Skills" tab. Top right: a small circular minimap labeled "Four Gates" with restrained brass ring. A tasteful small RL at upper edge. Keep the same overhead player name with slim bars. Modernization emphasizes hierarchy, empty space and legibility without losing the original practical fantasy game feeling. Warm ivory type, subdued emerald/blue resource colors, matte brass rules. Subtle fantasy engraving only at panel corners. This is a real intermediate step, not the radical layouts of the later concepts.
variants.review: Pass as an intermediate visual exploration. Preserves brass/brown palette and long bottom icon row while adding corner party/navigation groups. Generated objectives, map art and party data are illustrative. More ornamented than the prompt's restrained ideal.

DESIGN 03, MODULAR MMO, 60 percent redesign. A contemporary polished PC MMORPG interface using modern modular layout principles, inspired by the readability and grouping of modern World of Warcraft and FFXIV, but with original Rabbit Lands identity and no copied graphic assets. Completely REMOVE original right-side vertical rail and full-width bottom icon slab. Group vital information near the lower center, just above the hotbar: Health, Ether and Action as three clearly labeled slim horizontal bars with values, Food and Load as small secondary labeled indicators. Bottom center: TWO orderly rows of 8 beautifully painted square action/item/spell icons, consistent warm brass thin edges, clear keyboard hints 1-8 on first row, distinct cooldown sweep on just one icon, small quantity count on a potion. Small XP line beneath. Lower right edge: tiny monochrome utility menu icons for inventory, character, skills, crafting, journal and settings.
Upper left: compact party roster Kellan / Mira / Rowan, thin green health and blue ether bars, understated frames. Top right: a large enough readable circular minimap with area label "Four Gates"; below it a compact objective tracker "Meet at the bridge" and "Four Gates" with a small gold diamond. Lower left: restrained translucent tabbed Chat, 3-4 lines; a single separate subdued System event. At upper middle, a minimal slim target panel with NPC name "Rowan" for testing targeting hierarchy. Tiny overhead player name, no large black box over gameplay. Charcoal brown surfaces, small antique gold accents, cream sans-serif text with restrained serif area headings. Premium organized PC MMO finish, with sufficient breathing room around every cluster. About 80 percent of the courtyard still unobstructed. Balanced, practical, excellent information hierarchy, clear difference from the first two.
variants.review: Pass as a modular visual exploration. Centered resources and two hotbar rows, corner party/map, small menu, open courtyard. Gameplay abilities, cooldowns and XP shown are illustrative and do not define new systems.

DESIGN 04, PAINTERLY ADVENTURE, 80 percent redesign. An original expressive fantasy MMORPG HUD inspired by painterly action-MMORPG grouping, hand-brushed panel edges and a striking central health focus. Completely replace original bottom slab and right vertical rail. Preserve exact gameplay scene but frame it with a warm artisan-made interface.
Bottom center: a modest circular emerald Health medallion reading "120 / 150", antique brass silhouette with restrained leaf-inspired corner details. Five square hand-painted ability/item slots to its left and five to its right, unified single row, small keyboard hints. Ether and Action are thin teal and amber arcs beneath the medallion. Food and Load are compact text/icon meters below the outer ends, small XP hairline at bottom. Never let health medallion grow into an oversized illustration. Lower RIGHT: a square parchment-toned cartographic minimap with soft ink-edged border, "Four Gates" label, player arrow and sparse route marks; a tiny utility menu just beneath. Upper left: three quiet party rows with small round portraits/initials and brush-ended health bars. Upper right: a floating elegant quest/objective card with small brass diamond and "Meet at the bridge". Lower left: transparent chat text with just a few channel tabs on a feathery dark gradient; tiny System message beside it.
Visual language: matte painterly dark umber washes, warm cream typography, muted antique brass, teal/emerald resource accents; selected headings use a well spaced readable serif, body type is clear sans. Minimal restrained hand-made edges, high-quality painted fantasy icons and original small RL mark. Artisan fantasy identity, no rococo baroque clutter, no massive ornate wings, no sci-fi geometry. Large clear center for navigating the courtyard. Distinctive and contemporary while matching stylized Rabbit Lands world art.
variants.review: Pass as an expressive visual exploration. Central health medallion, flanking hotbar and parchment minimap give a distinct fantasy direction. Generated overhead bars remain from reference. Health styling, map and objectives need normal UI specification before implementation.

DESIGN 05, MINIMAL MODERN, 100 percent redesign. A radically restrained premium MMORPG HUD with flat contemporary typography and thin floating controls; original fantasy interface with neutral charcoal transparency, warm off-white text, single muted teal accent and tiny champagne gold hints. Completely abandon the old bronze right rail, bevels, square icon slabs, large player overhead bars, ornamental fantasy frames and two clocks.
Top center: very thin navigation compass ribbon with small N/E/W ticks and one gold diamond marker, with "Four Gates" as a small precise area label. Top left: tiny RL monogram plus a quiet three-row party list (Kellan, Mira, Rowan), slim color bars and initials, no framed container. Top right: compact clean rounded-square minimap and a single readable two-line objective "Meet at the bridge" / "Four Gates", aligned with clear spacing, no bulky background.
BOTTOM CENTER: a very compact 8-slot action ribbon, squared-off softly rounded translucent tiles with beautifully simplified original fantasy icon glyphs and tiny keyboard hints, one cooldown number. Slim Health and Ether bars immediately ABOVE it, labeled numeric values, with a smaller Action hairline; Food and Load in two tidy understated text indicators flanking it, XP as a fine accent line beneath. Lower right edge: six tiny lightweight utility glyphs for inventory / character / skills / crafting / journal / settings, with enough separation to be clickable. Lower left: three lines of transparent readable social chat, small channel chips and a faint input cue; one subdued System line. Player has only a tiny name "Kellan" above the model.
Make a coherent sophisticated flat UI, excellent contrast and typography, confident negative space, crisp alignment. No pill-heavy mobile dashboard cards, no neon sci-fi, no web page, no pixel font, no decorative flourishes. The same muted cobblestone game scene should visibly dominate 85-90 percent of the screen. This must look radically lighter and more contemporary than the previous four, but still fully functional for a mouse-and-keyboard fantasy MMORPG.
variants.review: Pass as a complete minimal visual exploration. Original slab/rail removed; flat controls, compact resource and action area, compass and open scene. Tiny resource and utility symbols need labeling/accessibility review before implementation.

review_scope: Visual HUD exploration, not production-ready UI specification or runtime asset replacement.
